selection: For the personal-profile slate, prioritize the first two coin topics; preserve tech variety with the next two. For a tech-only slate, select priorities 3 and 4. This is topic selection advice, not a production or scheduling instruction.

topics.topic: The three letters on some 1909 Lincoln cents
topics.hook: Why do some 1909 pennies have these three letters?
topics.payoff: Explain the V.D.B. placement/change with documented history and matched real specimens.
topics.openingProof: Real readable V.D.B. reverse crop with a small location label at frame zero, exact hook visible; pull back to the coin.
topics.cta: Would you check the date or the initials first?
topics.why: Combines a successful coin-detail question with the Lincoln audience lead.
topics.novelty: Existing Lincoln article covers presidential portrait adoption, not a complete initials-location/removal lesson.
productionConditions: Locate and identify owner-approved VDB and comparison coin images; never generate or alter details.
Map removal and restoration history to primary documentation before narration approval.
Do not imply every early 1909 cent carries the same mint mark or value.

topics.topic: Why the government sold its stored Carson City dollars
topics.hook: Why did the government auction silver dollars it had kept for decades?
topics.payoff: Explain the GSA sale and how packaging connects to the documented disposal process, without conflating it with the Pittman melting program.
topics.openingProof: Identified real GSA holder/coin beside a dated source excerpt; show the object and historical question together.
topics.cta: Would you investigate the coin or its government holder first?
topics.why: Tests the historical policy-paradox family that holds attention, rather than copying only the highest-view topic.
topics.novelty: Stored-coin disposal process is a distinct event from silver-dollar melting and replacement.
productionConditions: Source-check dates, inventory and sale mechanism with GAO/GSA records.
Require owner-approved matching coin and holder photography; no simulated coin details.

topics.topic: Check whether your custom-domain business email is DKIM signed
topics.hook: Your business email looks professional. Is it actually signed?
topics.payoff: Use a redacted test message to read the DKIM authentication result and explain its narrow meaning.
topics.openingProof: Readable DKIM result in a genuine redacted test header, labeled as actual test evidence; preserve the hook beside it.
topics.cta: Check the authentication result on one test email.
topics.why: Builds on email migration interest and practical business setup; platform counts remain separate.
topics.novelty: Message authentication is different from choosing Workspace, importing Gmail or configuring MX records.
productionConditions: Capture actual test headers, remove personal addresses and IDs.
Do not imply DKIM guarantees inbox placement, authentic intent or all-domain security.
Do not change live DNS during content preparation.

topics.topic: Unit price versus carton price in an AI-generated quote
topics.hook: Would your AI quote use the unit price or the carton price?
topics.payoff: Give one synthetic product row explicit units, quantity and price columns; compare a saved output to deterministic expected arithmetic.
topics.openingProof: Two clearly labeled price columns and the expected calculation, marked synthetic example; any AI output must be real saved output.
topics.cta: Label the units before asking AI to calculate.
topics.why: Turns broad input-quality and evidence themes into a concrete visual task.
topics.novelty: Specific unit/currency schema and arithmetic check, not another generic raw-material or prompting overview.
productionConditions: Check the existing raw-material lesson/transcript before final approval to avoid repeating its example.
Use synthetic data and show actual model output; do not invent a model mistake.
Record prompt, model/version, expected result and output.

topics.topic: Why deleting a leaked key does not revoke it
topics.hook: You deleted the leaked API key. Why can it still work?
topics.payoff: Explain removal versus credential revocation with a safe scoped test or clearly labeled diagram.
topics.openingProof: Redacted before/after authorization status, actual safe test if available; otherwise label the flow as illustrative.
topics.cta: Check which exposed credentials still need revoking.
topics.why: Retains a useful security sequel but ranks below stronger personal-profile topic families.
topics.novelty: Revocation after exposure, not browser variable placement or workflow secret access.
productionConditions: Keep earlier November 20 proposal and exact evidence trail.
No real production keys or unauthorized API changes.
Do not present Facebook and Instagram views as equivalent.
